newsitem.title: ITALY: IRI chief rules out TIM sale to cut debt.
newsitem.headline: IRI chief rules out TIM sale to cut debt.

text.p: Debt-laden Italian state industrial holding IRI on Tuesday ruled out the sale of Telecom Italia Mobile or the transfer to the Treasury of other assets that could be privatised as a way of cutting its borrowings.
Michele Tedeschi said in a statement that any asset transfer "would even constitute a form of evasion of objectives fixed in the well-known (European) community accord."
Under a 1993 deal, the European Commission established that IRI's debt should fall below five trillion lire by the end of 1996, compared with 22.46 trillion at end-1995.

An official in Brussels told Reuters that Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi had informed the European Commission that a capital injection would probably be needed for IRI before the end of the year. He had no details of size.
IRI has often said the only way it can meet the terms of its EU deal is via the sell-off of telecommunications holding Stet.
The company is slated for privatisation by March 31, 1997 but political filibustering is delaying creation of a telecoms watchdog, which must be set up before the sale goes ahead.
Tedeschi said that even if the Stet sale was delayed, a separate sale of TIM was not an option. TIM, Europe's biggest cellphone operator, was spun off from Stet in July 1995.
He said that rapid technological evolution of fixed-line and mobile telephony would reinforce ties between Stet and TIM.
"Any change would represent a total change of direction in a short time which could disorientate the markets and have a big negative impact on the credibility of the country," he said.
Government Undersecretary Enrico Micheli also ruled out a possible sale of TIM to reduce IRI's debts.
"If TIM were sold, the money would go to Stet and not to IRI," he said.
